name: Hook Text Design Sequence
use_when: The opening hook contains a short phrase that can become a scroll-stopping visual layout.
One keyword in the hook carries the main curiosity, result, identity, or contrast.
The edit needs a stronger first impression than ordinary captions provide.
The hook phrase can be reduced to a short problem/result statement that is easy to read while scrolling.
One word in the hook carries the emotional impact, result, or contrast and needs typographic hierarchy.
A branded intro needs short designed text for brand, proof, and outcome instead of ordinary subtitles.
avoid_when: The hook is already visually obvious from the footage or proof frame.
The hook phrase is too long to become a clean phone-size text design.
The design would hide the speaker's expression, product, proof, or key action.

timeline_pattern.pattern: hook_words -> select_key_phrase -> stack_text_layers -> balance_layout -> emphasize_keyword -> clear_or_transition_to_body
timeline_pattern.layer_rule: Use only the necessary hook words and extend those layers long enough to stack as a designed composition.
timeline_pattern.hierarchy_rule: One word or phrase should dominate; supporting words should frame it rather than compete.
timeline_pattern.impact_word_rule: Choose the word that changes the viewer's understanding or desire, not a filler word, as the strongest typographic element.
timeline_pattern.balance_rule: Check horizontal and vertical balance at phone size, not only in the desktop program monitor.
timeline_pattern.attachment_rule: In After Effects, parent hook text to the talking-head video only when it should scale with the zoom as if attached to the frame.
timeline_pattern.intro_text_rule: For branded intros, assign text roles to brand/show name, proof or authority quote, outcome phrase, and accent underline before animating.

motion.rule: Use restrained entrance motion or caption stack timing so the layout builds quickly without delaying the hook.

keyframe_values.hook_duration: Keep the designed hook inside the first 1-5 seconds for feed-first shorts.
keyframe_values.keyword_glow: Use glow or accent color only on the meaning-changing word; start with moderate threshold, radius around 90-100, and brightness around 125-135 if the glow remains readable.
keyframe_values.stack_timing: Layer words quickly enough to preserve spoken rhythm; avoid text still building after the viewer needs the claim.
keyframe_values.highlight_motion: Use Trim Paths 0 to 100 for underline/highlight strokes and ease the motion so the highlight lands with the word.
keyframe_values.typographic_contrast: Use weight, hue, case, or size contrast only where it clarifies the hook priority; avoid making all words equally loud.
keyframe_values.intro_flicker: Keep intro flicker or font-change accents to very short 3-9 frame bursts and only when the final word remains readable.

sound.rule: Use a subtle hit or whoosh only if it supports a real text entrance or keyword emphasis; keep speech dominant.

captions.rule: Remove or disable ordinary captions during the hook if the designed text already carries the same words.

color.rule: Use accent color to identify the keyword, but preserve contrast and avoid glow that blooms over nearby text.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use drawtext layers with timed enable expressions and optional glow via pre-rendered text assets; review phone-size contact sheets.
implementation.remotion: Represent hookText layers with text, hierarchy, x/y, startFrame, endFrame, emphasisStyle, and safeRegion fields.
implementation.blender: Use text objects in a 9:16 camera with simple scale/opacity keyframes and a single emphasized material.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Split the hook words into separate text layers, stack them in a balanced phone-safe layout, and emphasize the keyword with bold/color/glow.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Convert selected caption or text layers to graphics, stack them on separate tracks, arrange in Essential Graphics, and apply bold/color/glow to the keyword. In After Effects, animate hook text with slide/typewriter/highlight presets and parent text to the video when the zoom should carry it.

common_mistakes: Designing every hook word with equal weight.
Letting ordinary captions duplicate the designed hook text.
Making the layout pretty but too slow to read in the first seconds.
Using glow on the whole phrase instead of the keyword.
Covering the subject or proof that should support the hook.
Choosing a hook phrase that is too clever or long to read during the first scroll beat.
Emphasizing a visually convenient word instead of the impact word.
Letting brand, proof, outcome, and ordinary captions all compete in the same intro frame.
qc: The designed hook is understandable within the first five seconds.
One keyword or phrase has clear visual priority.
The layout does not duplicate ordinary captions unnecessarily.
Glow or accent color remains readable at phone size.
The hook text does not hide the face, product, proof, or key action.
Any parented hook text remains readable through the zoom.
The strongest typographic emphasis sits on the word that changes meaning or desire.
Intro text has clear brand, proof, outcome, and accent roles without duplicate captions.
